title: Volatility Surface Builder and Arbitrage Checker
context: Every derivatives desk and every serious options-adjacent interview involves the volatility surface: implied vol as a function of strike and expiry. Building one end-to-end — from raw option quotes to a smooth, arbitrage-checked, interpolable surface — exercises numerical root-finding, market conventions, data pipelining and the honest handling of illiquid quotes. The result is a genuine portfolio piece: the same code a desk's infra team writes in miniature, with the corners cut visibly labelled.
problem: Given a table of option quotes (strike, expiry, bid, ask, type) on a single underlying, build the implied-volatility surface: (1) invert Black-Scholes per quote with a bracketed, hybrid solver; (2) construct a parameterised fit in (log-moneyness, expiry) that is smooth by construction; (3) verify no static arbitrage — no negative call butterflies (convexity in strike) and no negative calendar spreads (forward variance non-negativity); (4) expose a clean API: `surface.vol(strike, expiry)` interpolated at arbitrary points, with documented error behaviour outside the quoted range. Handle quotes with zero or crossed markets honestly (skip, never invent).
requirements: Implied-vol inversion: bisection to a bracket, then Newton with vega as derivative; documented convergence criteria and a hard iteration cap
Mid-quote input with a minimum-spread filter; quotes wider than a configurable threshold are excluded and logged
Surface fit: your choice of SVI parameterisation per slice (recommended) or a quadratic-in-log-moneyness baseline — but the arbitrage checks must run on the fitted surface, not the raw points

Static-arbitrage checks: butterfly (second derivative of call price in strike ≥ 0) and calendar (total variance non-decreasing in expiry at fixed forward moneyness); violations reported with locations, not silently patched
Interpolation in expiry: linear in total variance (the standard convention) with the reasoning documented
A CLI that takes a quotes CSV and an output path, and prints an arbitrage report plus summary statistics
Reproducible demo: a bundled synthetic quote set (generated, clearly labelled) that exercises every code path

milestones.title: Core pricing and inversion
milestones.detail: Black-Scholes price + vega; hybrid bisection/Newton solver with tests on known round-trips (vol in → price → vol out, to 1e-8).

milestones.title: Quote ingestion and hygiene
milestones.detail: CSV parsing, mid/spread logic, exclusion filters, logging of excluded quotes with reasons.

milestones.title: Single-slice fit
milestones.detail: One expiry: SVI (or quadratic) fit with a documented optimiser choice; plot fitted vs quoted vols for the report.

milestones.title: Arbitrage checks
milestones.detail: Butterfly and calendar tests on the fitted surface; violation report format; unit tests with a deliberately violating surface.

milestones.title: Surface assembly and interpolation
milestones.detail: Per-slice fits joined by total-variance interpolation in expiry; `vol(K, T)` API with out-of-range policy.

milestones.title: CLI, demo data, write-up
milestones.detail: Command-line entry point, synthetic demo dataset, README with methodology and known limitations.

designGuidance.md: Structure the solver as a pure function `(quote, S, r, T) -> vol | None` so it can be vectorised or parallelised later without touching the fit layer.
Resist the temptation to interpolate implied vol directly in expiry: variance (or total variance) is the quantity that behaves linearly; the lesson material covers why.
Decide the out-of-range policy early and document it — extrapolated vols from an SVI fit can be nonsense; clamping, erroring and extrapolating-with-a-warning are all defensible, silence is not.

designGuidance.title: The arbitrage you must not patch away
designGuidance.md: When the checks fail, the temptation is to smooth harder until they pass. That hides the information: a genuine arbitrage in the fitted surface usually means a bad quote or a bad parameterisation, and the correct output is a *report*. Trading desks pay for the honest version.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Solver correctness and robustness (round-trip tests, failure handling)
Quote hygiene: exclusions justified and logged, never invented
Fit quality: sensible residuals, parameters in sane ranges
Arbitrage checks correct and *reported*, not patched
API design: vol(K, T) contract, out-of-range policy documented
Reproducibility: demo runs from clean checkout; decisions logged

documentationRequirements: Methodology: choice of parameterisation, optimiser, and interpolation convention with one-paragraph justifications
Arbitrage report format documented, with example output
Known limitations: extrapolation behaviour, liquidity assumptions, data hygiene scope
The honest-decisions log maintained from day one

Add time-slice weighting by open interest and show the effect on the surface's wings
